title: Frontend senior domain bundle splitting strategy
topic: Frontend senior domain bundle splitting strategy
question: At scale, how would you think about bundle size and code-splitting for a large web app with dozens of routes and many contributing teams?
idealAnswer:
Route-based code splitting is the baseline, each route's JS should load only when that route is visited, rather than shipping the entire app's code on first load

Beyond routes, split further on genuinely rarely-used or heavy code, like a rich text editor, a charting library, or a modal only some users trigger, loaded lazily on demand rather than in the main bundle

Watch for shared-dependency duplication across split chunks, if multiple lazy chunks each bundle their own copy of a large library, splitting can backfire, proper vendor/shared-chunk configuration avoids this

Set and enforce a performance/bundle-size budget in CI so a single PR can't silently regress load time, catching bloat before it ships rather than after users complain

Use real bundle analysis tools (like a bundle analyzer/treemap) to find and address unexpectedly large dependencies, rather than guessing, a single misused import can pull in a much larger library than intended

Consider that code-splitting has a UX cost too, waterfall requests for the split chunks introduce latency, and needs to be balanced against prefetching strategies (e.g. prefetching likely-next routes on hover or idle time)
